A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-transformer research. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, figures, tables, and relocated appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Tables 2–3 report original experiments on synthetic tumor-growth data and MIMIC-III-based semi-synthetic data.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original ablation, extended-horizon, and pseudo-outcome corruption results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The central GT architecture, generation/learning steps, loss, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix E.1 adds procedural variants: G-LSTM replaces the transformer backbone with an LSTM, while BT trains output heads directly on factual outcomes without G-computation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the tumor-growth and MIMIC-III semi-synthetic CAPO tasks. v2 extends coverage to weaker confounding (gamma = 6–9) and longer intervention sequences: tumor prediction horizons through 6 and MIMIC horizons through 12. No new dataset, population, or application domain is introduced.

E2.justification: CRN, TE-CDE, CT, RMSNs, and G-Net remain the comparators in Tables 2–3. Figures 4–6 additionally evaluate G-LSTM and BT against GT, including settings already reported in v1.

E3.justification: The original data generation, sample sizes, RMSE metric, tuning grids, and training budgets are retained. New protocols introduce controlled backbone/head variants and pseudo-outcome perturbations from 0.05 to 0.5 during training at tumor gamma = 10 and horizon 2 (Figure 7). Extended-horizon comparisons fix gamma = 10 or MIMIC N = 1000.

E4.justification: v1 reports benchmark variation across confounding, horizons, and sample sizes but no component ablations. Appendix E adds LSTM-backbone and no-G-computation controls to isolate architectural and adjustment contributions, plus a corruption experiment testing sensitivity to pseudo-outcome quality. Confounding and horizon analyses are also extended.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 retain mean RMSE and standard deviation over five seeds. New Figures 4–7 show uncertainty bands or error bars without defining them or stating their run counts. Consequently, the PDFs do not establish whether these retain the previous uncertainty-estimation practice or introduce a different one.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 are numerically unchanged. Figures 4–7 add substantial results for architectural variants, extended conditions, and corrupted pseudo-outcomes. For example, Figure 5 shows G-LSTM below GT in tumor RMSE at horizons 4 and 6, while Figure 7 shows increasing error under stronger corruption. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements in the retained GT scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds Propositions 1–2 and proof sections concerning iterative G-computation and GT's target, plus Proposition 3 comparing oracle IPW and G-computation pseudo-outcome variances. Sequential ignorability is expanded from one-step outcomes to future treatment sequences, and Appendix A corrects the final consistency substitution. These go beyond v1's existing G-computation derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace blanket 'unbiased' estimates with proper adjustment for time-varying confounding; Table 1 explicitly describes absence of infinite-data bias. This qualifies the claimed guarantee while retaining the regression-based G-computation novelty and low-variance contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the ablations as evidence of effectiveness across backbones, corruption sensitivity as evidence of pseudo-outcome quality, and decreasing tumor errors at longer horizons through heteroscedasticity. Appendix C extends its oracle variance comparison to GT versus RMSNs. v1's explicit limitations discussion about causal assumptions and heuristic tuning is removed, although the assumptions and tuning procedure remain documented.

D1.justification: v1's architecture, pseudocode, and implementation appendices reappear as v2 Appendices F–H with the same substantive details. Adam, validation-based tuning, hyperparameter grids, A100 hardware, runtimes, and code access information remain unchanged. Additional reproducibility settings for the new ablation models are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Frauen et al. (2024), 'Model-agnostic meta-learners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects over time,' and removes Ibrahim et al. (2024) on semi-supervised deep causal generative models. Appendices C–D elaborate the existing positioning against RMSNs and G-Net; the main research gap remains the same.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 revises bias terminology throughout, expands the pseudo-outcome and training explanations, replaces the Discussion section with a short conclusion, and inserts new appendix sections before the retained technical material. Citations switch to author–year style.

P2.justification: v2 adds a moment-dimension comparison table and four empirical figures: comparative line plots with shaded bands and a corruption bar chart. Some earlier benchmark results are redisplayed alongside new ablations. Original Figures 1–3 remain, while Table 1 labels, captions, title/author layout, typography, and page headers are revised.

improvement.justification: The G-LSTM/BT controls address v1's lack of evidence separating G-computation from the transformer backbone, and longer-horizon tests broaden empirical support. Qualifying the headline unbiasedness claim also improves precision. These gains are limited by removal of the explicit limitations discussion, undefined uncertainty displays, and new indexing and equation-reference errors in Section 4, including Equations 8–9. Overall, the added diagnostic evidence supports a modest net improvement.
